what_happened.line: The Select Board held a televised workshop with town committee chairs on goals, minutes-taking, agendas, volunteers and public communication.
Committee chairs from Finance, Parks, Assessors, Planning, Library, Cable, Council on Aging, ZBA and others reported on their goals and work.
Parks described fee changes, including swim lesson fees raised after years without an increase and an hourly turf field rental fee for outside groups.
The board took up the accounts payable warrant, but the vote outcome was not audible in the recording.
The board set its October meeting dates, then entered two executive sessions, one on the town manager's contract and one on union negotiations.

why_it_matters: Fees for the beach, turf field and cable service are paid directly by users and subscribers, and the discussion shows they are under review, including a cable franchise fee increase being negotiated with the cable provider.
The town manager's contract and union negotiations affect future town payroll costs, which are paid mostly from taxes, though no terms were stated in open session.
watch_next: Committees are to return the committee worksheet to the selectmen's office, and another mailing will go out.
The superintendent is to be approached about a School Committee workshop on long-term plans, on November 7 or 14.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the accounts payable warrant ($518,957.94), the $2.70 cable fee and the Monday Oct 23 meeting. Our minutes capture fee figures and a workshop plan that the official ones leave out. The main difference is the board roster: our "Rivas" matches no official member, and the dates and reasons around the Oct 23 meeting differ between the two records.
